whole_bank_confusability_ladder__near_du.label: same_mechanism_new_measurement
whole_bank_confusability_ladder__near_du.reason: Both run whole-bank-in-context versus top-k over a bank-size ladder with planted item composition and argue the crossover is a composition effect rather than prompt length, but B manipulates helpful instance-level near-duplicates across WebShop and ALFWorld where A manipulates harmful near-miss distractors on ALFWorld only, and their predictions about size-free composition effects diverge.

aggregate_or_comply__many_shot_averages_.label: same_mechanism_new_measurement
aggregate_or_comply__many_shot_averages_.reason: Both test whether an aggregating route (whole bank, compiled artifact) is robust to per-item bank noise while top-k retrieval complies with the items it injects, but A doses replay-validated wrong-procedure contamination and adds LLM- and rule-compiled playbook arms while B uses detours in the agent's own successes with step-count and imitation-signature readouts, so the two support different conclusions about which noise the routes differ on.

bindings_need_a_query_only_when_untestab.label: distinct
bindings_need_a_query_only_when_untestab.reason: Both plant hidden structure in ALFWorld with a wrapper to ask when a cached prompt still needs a query, but A's manipulated property is whether an instance binding can be tested at run time at fixed procedure count, while B's is the number of procedures and the size of the smallest compiled form; the mechanisms and the resulting rules for when retrieval is necessary are different.

recall_success_dissociation__archive:arc.label: distinct
recall_success_dissociation__archive:arc.reason: A manipulates retriever recall and duplicate availability and reports success residual over the best static prompt, whereas B holds the bank, query, k and retrieved items fixed and varies only the moment of injection, claiming stall-triggered reveal flips the sign of memory's effect; different independent variables and different claims.

many_shot_averages_detours__near_duplica.label: distinct
many_shot_averages_detours__near_duplica.reason: A attributes the whole-bank-versus-retrieval gap to per-item noise averaging (detoured self-pool trajectories) with retrieval committing to detours, while B attributes retrieval's bank-size advantage entirely to instance-level near-duplicates the in-context reader cannot locate in a growing haystack; different manipulations and opposite accounts of which route wins and why.

aggregate_or_comply__archive:archive:ret.label: distinct
aggregate_or_comply__archive:archive:ret.reason: A plants a controlled contamination rate to compare how retrieval, LLM/rule-compiled playbooks and whole-bank reading combine items, whereas B forbids planted conflicts, localizes harm in organically accumulated banks to disagreement within the retrieved set, and benchmarks read-time abstention gates against item-level filtering; different designs, outcomes and deliverables.

exemplar_lottery__recall_success_dissoci.label: distinct
exemplar_lottery__recall_success_dissoci.reason: A's claim is that retrieval's reported gain is the spread of the static exemplar draw distribution, tested by resampling fixed prompts and one-time curation rules, while B's is a recall-success dissociation governed by whether the retrieved binding is recoverable in-episode, tested by manipulating retriever recall and duplicate availability across two environments.

whole_bank_confusability_ladder__digest:.label: distinct

near_duplicate_needle_crossover__brief:W.label: distinct
near_duplicate_needle_crossover__brief:W.reason: B is only a design instruction to include a whole-bank long-context arm when the bank fits 16k; it asserts no claim about why retrieval beats whole-bank. compile_the_statistics_not_the_trajector.label: distinct

compile_the_statistics_not_the_trajector.label: distinct
compile_the_statistics_not_the_trajector.reason: B is a brief section heading enumerating environment properties that make retrieval necessary; it states no claim about compiled aggregate statistics beating retrieved trajectories, which is A's entire thesis.

relocated_bindings_demand__archive:archi.label: same_mechanism_new_measurement
relocated_bindings_demand__archive:archi.reason: Both hold that per-instance retrieval is decorative unless the retrieved content must vary with the instance, and that a fixed/compiled substitute then matches it; but A causally manipulates that condition by editing the PDDL initial state (binding demand) and the bank's same-scene supply, and tests a compiled location table, where B only measures retrieval-set Jaccard overlap and a frozen-subset swap.
